built.thesis: A Model is a frozen dataclass whose fields are its parameters, and a rung subclasses the rung it extends. The type's ladder is its class tree and the fallback is its MRO. built.best_when: Rungs really are refinements that nest their base (friction does), contributors write Python, and values flow into code as typed attributes that pyright checks (still 0 errors at pyright 1.1.390). Nesting is also what makes the held-out choice well posed: a subclass that reduces to its base is exactly where training error cannot choose and held-out error can. Inheritance gives the order for free, so the rule needs no separate ladder ranking.
built.loses_when: This loses in four cases. First, a choice between siblings (Stribeck or Load at M3): compare() orders only one chain, so it takes two comparisons against M2, and a tie between two siblings that both reach the floor is left to the user. Second, a rung that combines siblings (multiple inheritance gives a C3 fallback you may not mean). Third, non-Python consumers (robotparts JS/JSON, sim2real cards) cannot see a class. Fourth, "optional below, needed above" fields conflict with pyright for hand-declared M1 fields. Smaller costs: parameters share a namespace with the API, and a rung's fields are spread across 4-9 class bodies. The fit is unbounded: on servo B the overfit M3 lands at stribeck_velocity = -1.16.
keep_parts: Order the held-out choice by the fallback chain itself: sort candidates by fallback length and refuse a set that is not one chain (isinstance(upper, type(lower))). Any variant can do this with its own fallback().

A Comparison table that shows fit rms beside held-out rms and ÷ floor, in mN·m, with chosen = None when no rung reaches 1.5× floor ('climb a rung, or measure more'). It makes the overfit visible: on case B, M3 is 3.97 vs 4.04 on fit and 6.62 vs 4.33 held out.
Typed rung classes via PEP 681 dataclass_transform with __init_subclass__ registration and an import-time guard against v1's rung records (the ladder is found by declaration, so no registry).
built.migration: The plan is unchanged by the amendment and stays additive. score, compare and noise_floor are new API and touch no v1 record. Now: the classes sit beside v1's records and are checked against them at import, so tests/test_ladders_acceptance.py, the actuators/rungs/* bytes (robotparts' tools/sync_actuator_rungs.py and tests/core/test_actuator_rungs_vendored.py) and sim2real's tests/test_robot_models_parity.py (which reads ladders() live via holds/rung/fallback) are all untouched. Then: actuators/servo/ladder.py becomes LADDER = Ladder.from_classes(ServoModel), which builds each Rung from the classes (adds = a class's own required fields, optional = its defaulted ones, base = __bases__[0].key, with title, equation and references moved into the class body). ladders() keeps its signature, so sim2real's parity test and the ruler's per-rung assertions run unchanged. robotparts keeps vendoring model.py and model.json bytes, which do not move. The ruler needs edits only for what the classes don't hold yet (vocabulary, aliases, packed, deployment-only, wears, composes), landed first and alone. Selection parity: sim2real's parity rule 2 already checks that each card rung's base is in the mapped rung's fallback(), which here is the MRO that compare() walks. The 1.5 limit is copied, not imported (robot_models never reads sim2real), so add one assertion SELECT_LIMIT == TWINNED_LIMIT to sim2real's parity test when this lands.
built.new_rung_cost: 1) One class in the type's models module (servo.py), e.g. `class Dahl(CoulombViscous, level=3, name="dahl"):` with `dahl_stiffness: float` in its body. 2) While v1's records are the ruler, the matching Rung(...) record and a Parameter for dahl_stiffness in actuators/servo/ladder.py; the import-time guard refuses a class with no record. In the end state this shrinks to the Parameter. 3) To make it runnable, actuators/rungs/dahl/model.py and model.json. 4) Only if it adds a term the fit can't start linearly, a seeds() override (Stribeck's is 5 lines). Nothing is needed for selection: Dahl.fit(fit, start=m2) and ServoModel.compare([m1, m2, dahl], test) work as soon as the class exists, because compare() orders by the MRO and the floor rule belongs to the type.

built.best_when: Landing without breaking anyone matters most: the Family IS a v1 Ladder, so ladders() could hand out Families with no consumer edit. Also good when rungs keep arriving as robotparts-style model.py + model.json folders: binding, fitting and the held-out comparison against the floor all come free. And when the rung chosen in robot_models should be the same one sim2real twins, because both use the same select() rule and limit.
built.loses_when: The Model should stand alone. It can describe and compute itself, but fallback, siblings and choosing a rung all need its Family, and parameters are names in a dict that type checkers cannot see. The fitter has no physical bounds: on case B, M3 fits breakaway -4.73 N·m at 0.0107 rad/s. The held-out choice discards that fit, but nothing flags it on the BoundModel. Stateful (LuGre dt) or jointly nonlinear physics needs more than the linear/nonlinear probe. FLOOR_LIMIT duplicates sim2real's TWINNED_LIMIT, because robot_models cannot import sim2real.

built.best_when: Effects are orthogonal and you want combinations no rung names (stribeck + ripple, dcmotor on load friction) through + or redeclare, with no new rung. It also suits a ladder that is mostly 'fill the next slot', and a reviewer who wants each climb shown as one named slot swap. The held-out table makes 'this swap paid (20.28 → 1.00)' or 'did not pay (1.03 → 1.57)' a single row labelled with the slot it changed.
built.loses_when: It loses when effects inside one slot interact: stribeck AND load-dependent friction cannot be written as stribeck + load, so it needs a combined option or nested slots. It also loses when one rung spans slots (v1's drivetrain repeats ripple's harmonics), and when the fallback is not 'undo the last slot change'. The held-out rule needs a log with repeated plateaus (plateau ids) to read the floor from. Without them this compare cannot judge until the floor is stated some other way. The core is 347 lines, against a 250-line target.

Short of the floor, it climbs only to a child that beats the current rung held-out (Zach: if it doesn't improve test time performance, you are overfitting). Undo: drop the `reached` test in Family.climb.

built.best_when: The question is 'which rung does this unit's data justify, and with which numbers'. You have a rig log split into fit and held-out plateaus, and you want a defensible pick explained by a table of held-out rms against the rig's own noise floor, plus SI values ready for MuJoCo/sim2real. The 'what now' flow is three calls: from_datasheet, fit, climb.
built.loses_when:
- **Browsing or authoring the type.** Parameters are a dict, so type checkers see no fields.
- **Logs without repeated conditions.** The floor needs plateau ids; a free trajectory would need a floor passed in.
- **Siblings that need different experiments.** LuGre needs dt and M3.load needs tau_load, so one plateau log mostly prints 'skipped'.
- **Terms the plateaus never excite.** The climb then picks the lower rung, which is right for the data and wrong for the servo.
- **A rung that pays only as part of a pair.** The greedy climb can miss it.
- **Two copies of the 1.5 limit.** The selection rule is restated from sim2real, so it now lives in two repos.
keep_parts: Family.climb + Climb table: a greedy, tree-shaped version of sim2real's select(), judged on held-out data. Each row shows fit rms, held-out rms and ÷ floor, plus a verdict, and lists skipped rungs with their reason. It drops onto any variant's Family or Type kit.
noise_floor(log) framed as an estimator: the held-out rms of the 'knows every plateau mean' model, about 8 numpy lines with bincount. It is the yardstick the rule divides by.

The generic Levenberg–Marquardt fit over model.py: a warm start from the rung below, unit-scanned starting points, and sign canonicalisation for squared terms. It needs no per-rung fitting code and recovers the hidden truth from the fit plateaus alone.

The same as v1 today:
1. Add a Rung(level=3, name=..., base=..., adds=..., code="actuators/rungs/<word>", equation=..., references=...) to actuators/servo/ladder.py.

built.thesis: The Type is the entry point. It hands you a kit with its Models (the ladder), its Datasheet class, the rig Experiments that identify each Model, and its fidelity metric plus the rig's floor. So "datasheet + rig log, what now?" is servo.identify(fit, datasheet=ds), which returns every model those two cover and names the motion still missing. The kit owns the choice too: servo.compare(found, held_out) scores on plateaus the fit never saw and picks the lowest rung within 1.5x the floor.

decisions.label: Where the held-out comparison lives
decisions.value: In the Kit, next to the fidelity metric and the floor it divides by: Kit.compare(found, held_out). The type owns the metric, so it owns the choice, and every caller chooses the same way. The Model stays a declaration with values; it gets no score method.

decisions.label: Selection rule
decisions.value: sim2real's cards.schema.select(): the lowest rung whose held-out RMS ÷ the rig's pooled within-plateau std is at most TWINNED_LIMIT = 1.5. Same-level siblings are ranked by ratio, and chosen is None when no rung reaches the limit (the table then says to climb). No information criterion: the type already has a physical yardstick, the rig's repeatability.

decisions.label: compare refuses the fit log
decisions.value: Identified keeps the log it was fitted on (.log). compare raises ValueError when the held-out log shares a plateau with it. Choosing on training data is impossible, not merely discouraged. A plain dict of models, with no .log, still compares.

decisions.label: Training ratio shown, never chosen on
decisions.value: Comparison.on_fit puts the fit-plateau ratio beside the held-out ratio, so case B shows the overfit itself: M3 0.99 on fit and 1.57 held out, against M2 1.01 and 1.03.

decisions.label: Floor from plateau ids
decisions.value: The floor uses the log's plateau ids (pooled within-plateau std), the same formula the check uses, and falls back to exact speed repeats. The kit's held-out numbers match the oracle to two decimals (20.28, 1.00, 1.03, 1.57).

decisions.label: Coverage threshold 6 -> 5
decisions.value: COVERAGE now treats velocity_plateaus as at least 5 speeds held both ways. robotparts' '6-8 speeds' describes the whole rig run, and the alternating split leaves 5 of 10 speeds in the fit half. It is documented as a known gap: the real fix is to judge coverage on the run as a whole.

decisions.label: Honest finding
decisions.value: On this fixture, the 1.5x-floor rule would have picked M2 for case B even on training data, because M2 trains at 1.01x. A rule that takes the lowest training RMS picks M3 in both cases. Held-out data adds the evidence that M3 does worse on unseen plateaus, not just that it is unneeded; the check cannot tell this rule on fit data from the same rule on held-out data, and the refusal guard is what enforces held-out.

decisions.label: Case passed through, never branched on
decisions.value: run(case) binds case into the replayed session's namespace, and step 4 echoes it ('A'). Step 5b runs case B with literal rig_log("B", ...) calls so the transcript shows the negative control. run() asserts that the only error the session raises is step 5's ValueError refusal.

built.best_when: The question is "what do I run next, and when do I stop climbing?" A new part arrives, and the kit says which models the datasheet already gives, which rig motion unlocks which rung, and which rung is good enough, judged on held-out plateaus against the rig's own floor. The rule and the floor live in one place per type, so every caller (scenario, sim2real cards, robotparts) chooses the same way. That place matches how sim2real already organizes kits per type.
built.loses_when: You want the Model alone, or your own selection rule. Model parameters are a values mapping, not typed fields, so type checkers see nothing. A hand-built Model outside a kit is awkward because identified_by points at the kit's Experiment objects. The choice rule belongs to the kit, so a caller who wants AIC, a margin or another split has to go around compare: it takes the held-out log, never the rule. The rule restates sim2real's select() and its 1.5 limit, so two repos hold copies until one imports the other. A type with no rung folders gets no experiments and no fidelity metric.
keep_parts: Kit.compare(found, held_out) with the refusal guard: Identified remembers its fit log, and comparing on overlapping plateaus raises. This makes 'choose on test, not train' a property of the API, and it splices onto any variant whose fit returns an object.
The comparison table with a 'fit x floor' column beside 'held-out rms / floor / x floor / twinned', which shows overfitting on its own (case B: M3 0.99 on fit, 1.57 held out).
Identified.missing plus Experiment ids derived from robotparts' measured_by: 'M3.lugre: run small_reversals' is the 'what now' answer when no rung reaches the floor.

Landing it means adding src/robot_models/types.py plus two tests: every measured_by motion in a rung's model.json has a COVERAGE entry or is declared unreadable, and compare chooses on held-out plateaus (case A to M3.stribeck, case B to M2) and raises on the fit log. (2) robotparts vendoring of actuators/rungs/*: unchanged. The kit reads model.json and model.py read-only and exec's the rung source rather than importing it, so it leaves no __pycache__ and robotparts' byte-for-byte sha256 sync holds. (3) sim2real tests/test_robot_models_parity.py: unchanged; it reads ladders(), which stays. New coupling: Kit.compare restates sim2real's select() and TWINNED_LIMIT = 1.5, so landing should either share one constant (a parity assertion that both equal 1.5) or move select() into robot_models for sim2real to call. Later, sim2real's CameraKit and this Kit can converge on one shape. Rig logs passed to identify and compare need a plateau id per sample, or exact speed repeats as the fallback.

COVERAGE accepts 5 plateau speeds held both ways, not robotparts' 6-8, because the fit half of the alternating split holds 5; judging coverage on the whole run is left out. Physics runs for M0-M3 only: M3.load needs a tau_load input, M3.lugre runs at steady state, M3.weakening_capture is structure only, and M4-M7 are declared and raise on predict. The fitter is separable least squares (lstsq on levels and slopes, a scan plus golden-section search on one speed scale), numpy only; optional terms such as stribeck_exponent are defaulted, never fitted. The selection rule is a local copy of sim2real's select() and 1.5 limit, not an import. The module is type_kit.py, not robot_models.types, so it does not shadow the stdlib types module. Building every kit at import takes about 0.4 s.

v0.thesis: A Model is a frozen dataclass whose fields are its parameters, and a rung subclasses the rung it extends. So a type's ladder is its class tree, the fallback is the MRO, and a value is a typed instance that pyright and IDEs read field by field.
v0.shape:
Model  (frozen-dataclass base: PEP 681 dataclass_transform; __init_subclass__ applies @dataclass(frozen, kw_only))
└── ServoModel(Model, type="integrated_servo")   the TYPE = root class: tree() ladder() rung(key) canonical(alias) compare(models, log)
    ├── Ideal(level=0, name="ideal")   output_inertia: float, gear_ratio: float   (no default = the rung needs it)
    │   └── Datasheet(level=1, fields_from=IntegratedServo)   33 fields "= None" (read when stated)
    │       └── CoulombViscous(2)   coulomb_friction: float, viscous_friction: float  (redeclared without a default = needed from here)
    │           ├── Stribeck(3) breakaway_torque, stribeck_velocity, stribeck_exponent=None; overrides seeds()
    │           │   ├── LuGre(3) -> DcMotor(5)      └── WeakeningCapture(3) -> Drivetrain(4) -> Envelope(5) -> Wear(5) -> Residual(6)
    │           ├── Load(3)      └── Ripple(4)
    └── Learned(7)
class methods: fallback() = MRO as keys, needs(), reads(), parameter(name) from field metadata, alternatives(), describe(), from_datasheet(ds), fit(log, start=) -> Self

decisions.label: Ladder = class tree, found on definition
decisions.value: __init_subclass__ registers each rung class (level=, name= class keywords) with its type root, so there is no registry file. fallback() is the MRO read as keys. Same-level alternatives are the classes at the same level: Stribeck and Load are siblings, while LuGre and WeakeningCapture are Stribeck's M3 children.

decisions.label: Fields are parameters; metadata not retyped
decisions.value: A field with no default is needed and one with `= None` is read when stated. A subclass redeclares a field without a default to make it required. Unit and definition go into field.metadata['parameter'] from v1's vocabulary by name. A field named by an alias is refused at class creation (G4). M1's 33 optional fields are injected from IntegratedServo (fields_from=, PEP 0003 §6), so they are not typed twice; the cost is that type checkers don't see them.

decisions.label: One copy of physics and prose; guarded against v1
decisions.value: torque() loads today's actuators/rungs/<word>/model.py by path and loops it over numpy arrays. The reference's own term names (LuGre's sigma2) resolve through aliases. Title, equation and references are read from v1's Rung by key. At import, each class is checked against its v1 record (base, adds, optional), and all 14 keys match v1's fallback, needs and optional.

decisions.label: Fit is an alternative constructor
decisions.value: Stribeck.fit(log, start=m2) -> Stribeck (typed as Self). It runs a generic numpy Levenberg–Marquardt over the needed parameters the log moves, which it detects by perturbing each one. A rung that adds a nonlinear term overrides seeds(), like nn.Module.reset_parameters; Stribeck tries 6 stribeck_velocity starts spread geometrically over the logged speeds. compare() is a classmethod on the type root and picks the lowest BIC.

v0.best_when: Rungs are real refinements (each adds terms to its base, as friction does), the people adding rungs write Python, and values flow into code. Then IDE completion, pyright-checked constructors (missing parameter, alias keyword and frozen assignment are all caught; verified with pyright 1.1.390), dataclasses.replace/asdict, and `isinstance(m3, CoulombViscous)` all come for free.
v0.loses_when:
- **Two siblings combined:** a rung that combines siblings (Stribeck + load) needs multiple inheritance, and C3 linearizes it into a fallback you may not mean.
- **Optional below, required above:** pyright rejects redeclaring `x: float | None = None` as `x: float` ("overrides a field ... missing a default value"). Hand-declaring M1, the pure form, would raise 5 such errors; the prototype dodges them only by injecting M1's fields.
- **Non-Python consumers:** robotparts JS/JSON and sim2real cards can't see classes, so the ladder must be exported back to records.
- **Forced tree:** M7.learned extends nothing but still has to subclass the root.
- **Shared namespace:** parameters share the class namespace with the API (key, level, torque, fit), and nothing checks for collisions.
- **Scattered fields:** a rung's needs are spread across 4–9 class bodies; describe() gathers them back.
- **Size:** the core is 379 non-blank lines, above the 250 aim.
keep_parts: `dataclass_transform` on the base, with `__init_subclass__` applying `@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)` and filling each field's metadata from the type vocabulary. This makes parameters typed, IDE-visible attributes with no decorator; pyright confirms types, missing arguments, alias keywords and frozen assignment.

The import-time guard that checks each new-API object against its v1 Rung record (base, adds, optional). It makes any variant an additive layer: the ruler, the rung bytes, robotparts vendoring and sim2real parity stay untouched while both exist.

`fit(log, start=)` that frees only the needed parameters the log numerically moves (so datasheet inertia and ratio ride along), plus a per-rung `seeds()` hook for nonlinear terms. Also the tree printer that collapses single-child chains, putting all 14 rungs in 8 lines.
v0.migration:

decisions.label: Family subclasses v1's Ladder
decisions.value: A Family IS a Ladder plus .models, so every v1 call and check (fallback, canonical, parameters, holds, resolve, composed) is inherited unchanged; ladders() could return Families with no consumer edit.

decisions.label: Base stays a key; the Family owns the tree
decisions.value: A Model carries its resolved Parameter records (inherited ones included, with units and definitions), so it describes itself. Fallback, children, siblings and tree() are Family calls: the records are flat and the tree is data, not inheritance.

decisions.label: Physics attached from the unchanged rung folder
decisions.value: Physics.load compiles model.py from source; an import would write __pycache__ into a folder robotparts pins byte for byte. model.json gives the inputs, output, required terms and MuJoCo maps, translated to canonical names through the family's aliases (LuGre's sigma2 -> viscous_friction). Attached for M0-M3 only.

decisions.label: Fit on the Model, compare on the Family
decisions.value: Model.fit is generic separable least squares: it probes the physics to split terms into linear ones (solved by lstsq) and nonlinear ones (a log-spaced grid over the logged input range, refined 4x), then checks the linear terms superpose at the answer. Compare uses BIC and sits on the Family because it is a question about the tree.

v0.best_when: Landing without breaking anyone matters most. Three repos read ladders() today, and this layer is purely additive because its Family is a Ladder. It also suits rungs that keep arriving as robotparts-style folders (model.py + model.json): the record picks them up, and binding, fitting, comparison and the MuJoCo export come with no extra code.
v0.loses_when: You want the Model to stand alone and be typed. It can describe and compute itself, but fallback, siblings and comparison need its Family. Parameters are names in a vocabulary, not attributes a type checker sees (values is a dict). Stateful or non-separable physics outgrows the linearity probe: LuGre runs at steady state only, and a jointly nonlinear term needs an explicit grid=.
keep_parts: Model.fit: generic separable least squares probed on the physics itself. Any rung's model.py fits with no fitting code: linear terms by lstsq, nonlinear terms on a refined log grid spanning the logged range of the input that shares their unit, plus a check that the linear terms superpose at the answer.

Physics.load: compile + exec model.py from the pinned rung folder (no __pycache__) and read model.json's required terms, inputs and MuJoCo maps through the family's aliases. This gives BoundModel.mujoco() and fit's free set for free.
Family as a subclass of Ladder (zero-edit migration for the ruler, robotparts and sim2real), plus its compact tree(): single-child chains collapse to 'a → b' and * marks the runnable models.
v0.migration: To land it, add src/robot_models/family.py (family_records.py without RUNNABLE_UP_TO); nothing else changes. Optionally later, ladders() returns Family.from_ladder(...) and type folders write LADDER = Family(...). v1 ruler (tests/test_ladders_acceptance.py): untouched. Rung records, keys, bases, adds, the code strings and every rung byte stay as they are; isinstance(LADDER, Ladder) holds for a Family; the value scan judges type folders, not a root module; test_every_module_imports_in_a_fresh_interpreter picks up one more module (numpy is already a runtime dependency in pyproject). robotparts vendoring of actuators/rungs/*: untouched. The folders are read in place and exec'd from source, never imported, so no __pycache__ lands in them and the byte-identical folder test and the RUNG_FILES sha256 table stay green. sim2real tests/test_robot_models_parity.py: untouched. It calls ladders(), .keys, .rung(), .resolve(), .holds() and .composed(), all inherited by Family; sim2real can later fit through families()[t][key].fit(...) as an additive step.

decisions.label: A slot holds a whole law, not a delta
decisions.value: friction:stribeck includes Coulomb and viscous; it is not coulomb_viscous + a Stribeck excess, because LuGre and weakening_capture replace Stribeck rather than add to it. Terms add across slots and replace each other within one (Modelica replaceable, not lmfit + everywhere). M1.datasheet is a friction option, since a slot of its own would count friction twice under M2.

decisions.label: Derived from v1 and checked against it
decisions.value: A term's needs are what its own slot's rungs add down the v1 fallback. A preset is the nearest option per slot down that fallback. The Slots constructor raises unless all 14 presets match v1's parameters(), optional() and fallback() exactly. The type adds one table, SLOT_OF (word -> slot).

decisions.label: The ladder tree comes from the slots
decisions.value: Model.down() steps one term back within its slot or empties the slot, and must land on exactly one preset. This reproduces all 14 v1 base chains. For an off-ladder sum it reports the ambiguity instead of guessing.

decisions.label: Fit on the composite, with no per-rung fitting code
decisions.value: Model.fit nudges each parameter to find the unseen ones (carried from start), the linear ones (solved by lstsq) and the nonlinear ones (log grid over the log's own range when the unit matches an input, then zoomed). This is variable projection, numpy only. compare() uses BIC and labels each row by the slot it swapped.

decisions.label: Runnable cap by level
decisions.value: RUNNABLE_UP_TO = 3 follows the round's stop line, so M4.ripple stays declared even though its model.py exists (and would compose as a pure term, since it .get()s friction with a default of 0). Calling a declared term raises NotImplementedError with the reason.

v0.best_when: Effects are orthogonal and you want combinations no rung names (stribeck + ripple, dcmotor electrics on load friction) through + or redeclare without adding a rung. Also when most of the ladder is 'fill the next slot' (M4 to M6 are exactly that), and when a reviewer needs to see what differs between two models: changes() prints 'friction: coulomb_viscous → stribeck', and the preset × slot grid shows the whole ladder at a glance.
v0.loses_when: Effects inside one slot interact: Stribeck and load-dependent friction together cannot be written as stribeck + load, because both are friction options, so the combination needs a new option or nested slots. It also loses when one rung spans slots (v1's M4.drivetrain re-adds ripple's harmonics; the composed view surfaces this but keeps it as v1 has it), when a ladder's fallback is not 'undo one slot change', and when fitting needs more than two nonlinear unknowns or negative nonlinear parameters (the grid is logarithmic). Within this round's scope, the core is 320 lines plus a 27-line table, over the 250-line target.
keep_parts: Slots(ladder, SLOT_OF): a 27-line table plus a constructor that derives the presets from v1 and raises unless every preset's parameters, optional names and fallback equal v1's. Any variant could use it as a cheap bridge or ruler.

The preset × slot grid printout together with Model.changes(other) ('friction: coulomb_viscous → stribeck'). It makes the ladder readable at a glance and labels each comparison row by what was swapped.

The generic fit, which needs no per-rung code: numeric detection of unseen, linear and nonlinear parameters, lstsq for the linear ones, and a zooming log grid over the log's own range for the rest (variable projection, numpy only). Also the term-spelling map read from model.json, which passes viscous_friction to LuGre's model.py as sigma2.

decisions.label: get_params() returns the physical values
decisions.value: It returns every held value, stated and fitted, as {canonical name: SI}, unlike sklearn's split between hyperparameters and coef_. These values are what MuJoCo and sim2real get handed, and fitted_ (trailing underscore) says which ones the log set.

decisions.label: k counts fitted values only
decisions.value: A value the datasheet states costs the log nothing, so M1 is charged 0 and each rung pays ln(n) per term it adds above M1. Optional terms such as stribeck_exponent keep their default and are neither fitted nor charged.

decisions.label: One generic fit, no per-rung fitting code
decisions.value: Levenberg–Marquardt runs over model.py with a numpy forward-difference Jacobian. A value already held starts there (the datasheet's, or the rung below's in a climb). A missing torque starts at the log's torque scale, and a missing speed is scanned over the log's speeds. A term whose sign the log cannot see is reported positive: without this, the warm-started climb returned stribeck_velocity = −0.249.

decisions.label: The climb is greedy over children, with a BIC margin of 2
decisions.value: At each step every rung extending the current one competes, and the best moves up only if ΔBIC < −2 (Kass & Raftery 1995). A rung the log cannot feed (a missing input column, or declared physics) is listed as skipped with its reason, not dropped silently.

v0.best_when: The question is "which rung does this unit's rig log justify, and with which numbers". You get a defensible pick backed by a BIC table, plus SI values ready for a simulator, in three calls (from_datasheet, fit, climb). It suits batch identification of many units of one type and CI that re-identifies whenever a new log lands.
v0.loses_when:
It loses in four cases:
- The job is browsing or authoring the type: parameters are a dict, so type checkers see no fields, and the metadata is reached through the model and family.
- Sibling rungs need different experiments: LuGre needs a dt time series and the load rung needs tau_load, so one plateau log mostly prints "skipped".
- Residuals are correlated, as they are on one real plateau: i.i.d. BIC then over-rewards added terms unless plateau means are fitted.
- A higher rung pays only as part of a pair: the greedy climb can miss it.

Fitting is also slow, about 1–3 s per M3 fit, because predict loops over the scalar stdlib model.py.
keep_parts: Family.climb(datasheet, log) and its report table (k, rms, BIC, ΔBIC, and a verdict or skip reason per rung). It needs only fit/predict on a Model, so it can sit on top of any variant.
Model.from_datasheet(ds, key), which finds the family from the datasheet's class, plus set_params resolving aliases to canonical names and converting alias units to SI.

The generic fit: Levenberg–Marquardt over the unchanged model.py, with term names resolved through aliases (LuGre's sigma2), unit-aware starting scans and sign-invisible terms reported positive. No rung writes fitting code.
v0.migration:
This is an additive layer that changes no bytes. It reads robot_models.ladder.ladders() (Ladder, Rung, Parameter, Alias) and actuators/rungs/<word>/model.py and model.json, and would ship as robot_models/estimators.py beside ladder.py.
- v1 ruler (tests/test_ladders_acceptance.py): untouched, because the ladder data, keys, aliases and rung-folder bytes it pins do not change. A new test file would hold the new grade: on a simulated log, M3 recovers a hidden Stribeck truth, and the climb picks M3 on the full log and M2 on fast plateaus only.
- robotparts vendoring of actuators/rungs/*: untouched. model.py and model.json are only read (inputs, terms), never rewritten, so the implementation_sha256 values in model.json and the ruler's byte check stay valid. Term names such as sigma2 are resolved through the ladder's aliases, not edited.
- sim2real tests/test_robot_models_parity.py: untouched, since it checks card names against ladder.resolve() and holds(), which are unchanged. As a later opt-in, sim2real could take model.get_params() (canonical names, SI) instead of mapping fitted values itself.
v0.new_rung_cost:
The same as v1 today, and nothing more:
1. One Rung(level=3, name=..., base=..., adds=(...), code="actuators/rungs/<word>", equation=..., references=...) entry in actuators/servo/ladder.py.
2. The folder actuators/rungs/<word>/ with model.py (torque(terms, inputs, state, dt)) and model.json (inputs, terms).

It then appears in the tree automatically, from_datasheet fills it, and fit() estimates its required terms above M1. The climb tries it as a child of its base and keeps it only if it pays on BIC. The one exception is a rung that least squares cannot fit, such as one needing a special experiment or bounded terms: it would need a per-rung fit override, and that hook is not built.
v0.simulated:
- Runnable physics stops at M0–M3: M4–M7 raise NotRunnable with the reason, and M3.weakening_capture has no physics shipped.

- predict loops in Python over the scalar stdlib model.py: arrays go in and come out, but it is not truly vectorized.
- The rig log is the fixture's simulated plateaus with i.i.d. noise, and the variant never reads the hidden values.
- BIC assumes independent Gaussian residuals.
- Starting points chosen by unit are a heuristic.
- Not built:
  - parameter covariance or uncertainty, and cross-validation;
  - composition across types (M4.drivetrain composes foc_controller);
  - a per-rung fit override hook;
  - full sklearn compliance (clone, check_estimator): fit takes a dict of columns, not (X, y).

v0.thesis: The Type is the entry point and hands you a kit with everything it has: its Models (the ladder), its Datasheet class, the Experiments (rig motions from robotparts' measured_by) that identify each Model's parameters, and its fidelity metric. decisions.label: Experiments are per model and per parameter, read from model.json
decisions.value: Each parameter's identifying experiment comes from robotparts' measured_by on that rung, falling back down the chain. The same coulomb_friction is 'reading the datasheet' on M1 and 'velocity plateaus' on M2. identify() asks whether the log is that motion (Experiment.covers), then whether the datasheet states the parameter; otherwise the model goes to .missing with 'run <motion>'. The only new data is COVERAGE: what counts as each motion (for example, 6 or more plateaus held both ways). Motions it cannot read say so.

decisions.label: Fitting lives in the kit and calls the rung's own physics
decisions.value: Separable least squares. Levels (N·m) and slopes enter linearly and are solved by lstsq, with columns evaluated through model.py. The one speed scale (rad/s) is scanned over the speeds the log held, then refined by golden section. Superposition is checked at the answer, so a rung outside this form fails loudly. Optional terms (stribeck_exponent) are read or defaulted, never fitted. numpy only.

decisions.label: The fidelity metric chooses, not an information criterion
decisions.value: The kit picks the lowest rung within 1.5x the rig's within-plateau scatter (sim2real's TWINNED_LIMIT): the climb stops where the rig cannot tell model from part. On the fixture: M0 131x, M1 57x, M2 17x (M2's fitted viscous_friction comes out negative while it imitates the Stribeck drop), M3 0.99x.

decisions.label: Rung code is exec'd from source, never imported
decisions.value: An import would leave __pycache__/ in a vendored rung folder whose file set robotparts hashes byte for byte (PEP 0004 §8.1). The kit reads model.json and model.py read-only. Alias terms (LuGre's sigma2) are mapped through Ladder.resolve.

v0.best_when: The question is "what do I run next?". A part arrives with a datasheet, and the kit says which models the datasheet already gives, which rig motion unlocks which rung, what the log identified, and when to stop climbing. One object per type also matches how sim2real assigns types to a robot (CameraKit / kits_for), so camera, depth and HSI kits can share the shape.
v0.loses_when: You want the Model on its own, or typed parameters. A Model still has its physics and card, but its identified_by points at the kit's Experiment objects, so building one outside a kit is awkward. Values are a Mapping, so type checkers see nothing (weak on fr6 against a dataclass-per-rung design). The kit is also only as rich as model.json: types with no rung folders (camera, conveyor, ...) get models and a tree, but no experiments and no fidelity metric. The core runs to 330 non-blank lines, over the 250 aim; about 75 of them print the tree, the card and the tables.
keep_parts: Experiment derived per (model, parameter) from model.json measured_by, plus identify() returning .missing {key: 'run <motion>'}: the concrete 'what now' answer (type_kit.py Experiment, COVERAGE, Kit.identify)

fit_plateaus: a separable least-squares fitter that builds its lstsq columns from the rung's own model.py and checks superposition at the answer, so no equation is retyped. It drops into any variant's fit.

Choose by the fidelity floor: the lowest rung within 1.5x the rig's within-plateau scatter (sim2real TWINNED_LIMIT). Also _physics(): exec model.py from source so the vendored rung folders never get a __pycache__.
